thesis: This pick carries the market's own probability and no edge, by construction. It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

Its p_model is the board's own de-vigged consensus for this exact selection, republished unchanged by analyze()'s PROJECT phase under the identity map -- zero fitted parameters, no recalibration intercept, no Platt, no isotonic refit (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md §2). Because the probability IS the price, diffing the two would measure nothing: edge_bps is structurally None and no edge is claimed. It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

Its p_model is the board's own de-vigged consensus for this exact selection, republished unchanged by analyze()'s PROJECT phase under the identity map -- zero fitted parameters, no recalibration intercept, no Platt, no isotonic refit (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md §2). Because the probability IS the price, diffing the two would measure nothing: edge_bps is structurally None and no edge is claimed. It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

mechanism_predicates.claim: the ground-ball starter this side is backed behind actually pitched to the ground, at or above the league share of unambiguous batted-ball outs
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_batted_balls

thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (starter_groundball_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 41.8%, home 58.3% (this game's own values rest on: away over 773 batted balls; home over 1,963 batted balls); a gap of 16.5 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 11.6 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 44faa9639a3a54e8.)

thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) this lineup's measured production against the primary pitch of the starter it faces (lineup_vs_primary_pitch; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.365 wOBA, home 0.315 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 5,119 plate appearances; home over 347 plate appearances); a gap of 0.051 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.029 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,048 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter who leans on one pitch, against a lineup that has measurably hit that pitch, has nowhere to hide for eighteen outs; the market prices his season line, not tonight's specific collision. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. mechanism_predicates.claim: the lineup that has measurably hit this starter's primary pitch reaches base against him at or above the league rate starters allow -- 'nowhere to hide for eighteen outs', measured over the outs he actually got
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) this lineup's measured production against the primary pitch of the starter it faces (lineup_vs_primary_pitch; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.365 wOBA, home 0.315 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 5,119 plate appearances; home over 347 plate appearances); a gap of 0.051 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.029 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,048 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter who leans on one pitch, against a lineup that has measurably hit that pitch, has nowhere to hide for eighteen outs; the market prices his season line, not tonight's specific collision. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 5f6d68dec562b5b3.)

thesis: This is a DELIBERATE CONTROL, not a pick anyone should follow: it takes the home side of the run line in every game, always, on no information at all. The direction was fixed in code before any board was read and is never derived from price, a clock or a search. Its p_model is a declared coin flip (provenance=placeholder), so no edge_bps can ever be computed for it -- that is the point: it is the baseline every real system has to beat (src.engine.adapters.evolab_system).

counterarguments.detail: books_at_decision=0 < 2
DEGRADED_INFORMATION: away_lineup: not present in assumption_exposure; home_lineup: not present in assumption_exposure; home_plate_umpire: not present in assumption_exposure

thesis: This pick carries the market's own probability and no edge, by construction. Its p_model is the board's own de-vigged consensus for this exact selection, republished unchanged by analyze()'s PROJECT phase under the identity map -- zero fitted parameters, no recalibration intercept, no Platt, no isotonic refit (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md §2). Because the probability IS the price, diffing the two would measure nothing: edge_bps is structurally None and no edge is claimed. It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

mechanism_predicates.claim: the lineup that has measurably hit this starter's primary pitch reaches base against him at or above the league rate starters allow -- 'nowhere to hide for eighteen outs', measured over the outs he actually got
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) this lineup's measured production against the primary pitch of the starter it faces (lineup_vs_primary_pitch; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.348 wOBA, home 0.394 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 5,122 plate appearances; home over 3,125 plate appearances); a gap of 0.046 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.029 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,048 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter who leans on one pitch, against a lineup that has measurably hit that pitch, has nowhere to hide for eighteen outs; the market prices his season line, not tonight's specific collision. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 5f6d68dec562b5b3.)

mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 31.7%, home 50.1% (this game's own values rest on: away over 6,139 pitches; home over 6,747 pitches); a gap of 18.4 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 16.3 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. mechanism_predicates.claim: the lineup that has measurably hit this starter's primary pitch reaches base against him at or above the league rate starters allow -- 'nowhere to hide for eighteen outs', measured over the outs he actually got
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) this lineup's measured production against the primary pitch of the starter it faces (lineup_vs_primary_pitch; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.348 wOBA, home 0.394 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 5,122 plate appearances; home over 3,125 plate appearances); a gap of 0.046 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.029 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,048 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter who leans on one pitch, against a lineup that has measurably hit that pitch, has nowhere to hide for eighteen outs; the market prices his season line, not tonight's specific collision. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 5f6d68dec562b5b3.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the lineup facing the one-pitch-heavy starter reaches base against him at or above the league rate starters allow -- predictability showing up as production
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 31.7%, home 50.1% (this game's own values rest on: away over 6,139 pitches; home over 6,747 pitches); a gap of 18.4 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 16.3 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 11da2d044a08ac38.)

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 2 pre-registered signals fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 31.7%, home 50.1% (this game's own values rest on: away over 6,139 pitches; home over 6,747 pitches); a gap of 18.4 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 9.7 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. (2) the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (starter_groundball_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 48.1%, home 38.0% (this game's own values rest on: away over 1,069 batted balls; home over 1,161 batted balls); a gap of 10.1 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 6.5 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 60.9%, home 43.0% (this game's own values rest on: away over 3,829 pitches; home over 6,582 pitches); a gap of 17.9 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 16.3 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome e64c85130b4664cc.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the harder-throwing starter -- the one this side is backed BECAUSE its opponent has to face him -- holds that opposing lineup below the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (starter_velocity_gap; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 6.58 mph, home -1.20 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 238 measured fastballs; home over 216 measured fastballs); a gap of 7.78 mph, clearing the threshold of 3.38 mph (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 375833d79e4bfef1.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the harder-throwing starter -- the one this side is backed BECAUSE its opponent has to face him -- holds that opposing lineup below the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (starter_velocity_gap; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 6.58 mph, home -1.20 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 238 measured fastballs; home over 216 measured fastballs); a gap of 7.78 mph, clearing the threshold of 3.38 mph (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 375833d79e4bfef1.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the platoon-advantaged lineup reaches base against the starter it was posted against at or above the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (lineup_platoon_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 44.4%, home 66.7% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 22.3 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 4703ed67882a9d2b.)

Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (starter_groundball_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 30.1%, home 42.9% (this game's own values rest on: away over 299 batted balls; home over 1,444 batted balls); a gap of 12.8 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 11.6 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (lineup_platoon_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 44.4%, home 66.7% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 22.3 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. mechanism_predicates.claim: the platoon-advantaged lineup reaches base against the starter it was posted against at or above the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (lineup_platoon_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 44.4%, home 66.7% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 22.3 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 4703ed67882a9d2b.)

This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) this lineup's measured production against the primary pitch of the starter it faces (lineup_vs_primary_pitch; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.350 wOBA, home 0.382 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 5,172 plate appearances; home over 5,557 plate appearances); a gap of 0.031 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.029 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,048 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter who leans on one pitch, against a lineup that has measurably hit that pitch, has nowhere to hide for eighteen outs; the market prices his season line, not tonight's specific collision. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 5f6d68dec562b5b3.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the lineup that has measurably hit this starter's primary pitch reaches base against him at or above the league rate starters allow -- 'nowhere to hide for eighteen outs', measured over the outs he actually got
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) this lineup's measured production against the primary pitch of the starter it faces (lineup_vs_primary_pitch; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.350 wOBA, home 0.382 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 5,172 plate appearances; home over 5,557 plate appearances); a gap of 0.031 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.029 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,048 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter who leans on one pitch, against a lineup that has measurably hit that pitch, has nowhere to hide for eighteen outs; the market prices his season line, not tonight's specific collision. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 5f6d68dec562b5b3.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the lineup facing the one-pitch-heavy starter reaches base against him at or above the league rate starters allow -- predictability showing up as production
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 39.1%, home 24.1% (this game's own values rest on: away over 8,639 pitches; home over 3,063 pitches); a gap of 15.0 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 9.7 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 6093c1cf8a6d6c08.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the lineup facing the one-pitch-heavy starter reaches base against him at or above the league rate starters allow -- predictability showing up as production
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 39.1%, home 24.1% (this game's own values rest on: away over 8,639 pitches; home over 3,063 pitches); a gap of 15.0 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 9.7 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 6093c1cf8a6d6c08.)

thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 39.1%, home 24.1% (this game's own values rest on: away over 8,639 pitches; home over 3,063 pitches); a gap of 15.0 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 9.7 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome e7f41ed66082c279.)

This pick carries the market's own probability and no edge, by construction. Its p_model is the board's own de-vigged consensus for this exact selection, republished unchanged by analyze()'s PROJECT phase under the identity map -- zero fitted parameters, no recalibration intercept, no Platt, no isotonic refit (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md §2). Because the probability IS the price, diffing the two would measure nothing: edge_bps is structurally None and no edge is claimed. It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

Its p_model is the board's own de-vigged consensus for this exact selection, republished unchanged by analyze()'s PROJECT phase under the identity map -- zero fitted parameters, no recalibration intercept, no Platt, no isotonic refit (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md §2). Because the probability IS the price, diffing the two would measure nothing: edge_bps is structurally None and no edge is claimed. It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

mechanism_predicates.expected: top_minus_bottom_reached_base_rate > 0, over at least 6 plate appearances per order half
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) this lineup's top-of-order minus bottom-of-order strength (top_minus_bottom; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.001 wOBA, home 0.035 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 8,964 plate-appearance denominators; home over 8,181 plate-appearance denominators); a gap of 0.034 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.023 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,838 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a top-heavy order concentrates its best bats where the extra plate appearances go, and club-level pricing averages that concentration away; the weakest mechanism of the six, kept because V4 stated it before seeing its result. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome e7f41ed66082c279.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the top-heavy order's first four slots out-reach its own bottom five against the starter they faced -- the concentration the mechanism claims, in the innings it claims it for
mechanism_predicates.expected: top_minus_bottom_reached_base_rate > 0, over at least 6 plate appearances per order half
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) this lineup's top-of-order minus bottom-of-order strength (top_minus_bottom; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.001 wOBA, home 0.035 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 8,964 plate-appearance denominators; home over 8,181 plate-appearance denominators); a gap of 0.034 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.023 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,838 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a top-heavy order concentrates its best bats where the extra plate appearances go, and club-level pricing averages that concentration away; the weakest mechanism of the six, kept because V4 stated it before seeing its result. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) this lineup's top-of-order minus bottom-of-order strength (top_minus_bottom; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.001 wOBA, home 0.036 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 8,964 plate-appearance denominators; home over 8,181 plate-appearance denominators); a gap of 0.036 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.023 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,838 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). mechanism_predicates.claim: the top-heavy order's first four slots out-reach its own bottom five against the starter they faced -- the concentration the mechanism claims, in the innings it claims it for
mechanism_predicates.expected: top_minus_bottom_reached_base_rate > 0, over at least 6 plate appearances per order half
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) this lineup's top-of-order minus bottom-of-order strength (top_minus_bottom; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.001 wOBA, home 0.036 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 8,964 plate-appearance denominators; home over 8,181 plate-appearance denominators); a gap of 0.036 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.023 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,838 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a top-heavy order concentrates its best bats where the extra plate appearances go, and club-level pricing averages that concentration away; the weakest mechanism of the six, kept because V4 stated it before seeing its result. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome e7f41ed66082c279.)

Its p_model is the board's own de-vigged consensus for this exact selection, republished unchanged by analyze()'s PROJECT phase under the identity map -- zero fitted parameters, no recalibration intercept, no Platt, no isotonic refit (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md §2). Because the probability IS the price, diffing the two would measure nothing: edge_bps is structurally None and no edge is claimed. It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

mechanism_predicates.claim: the top-heavy order's first four slots out-reach its own bottom five against the starter they faced -- the concentration the mechanism claims, in the innings it claims it for
mechanism_predicates.expected: top_minus_bottom_reached_base_rate > 0, over at least 6 plate appearances per order half
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) this lineup's top-of-order minus bottom-of-order strength (top_minus_bottom; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.001 wOBA, home 0.036 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 8,964 plate-appearance denominators; home over 8,181 plate-appearance denominators); a gap of 0.036 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.023 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,838 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a top-heavy order concentrates its best bats where the extra plate appearances go, and club-level pricing averages that concentration away; the weakest mechanism of the six, kept because V4 stated it before seeing its result. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome e7f41ed66082c279.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the ground-ball starter this side is backed behind actually pitched to the ground, at or above the league share of unambiguous batted-ball outs
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_batted_balls

thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (starter_groundball_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 42.9%, home 50.1% (this game's own values rest on: away over 1,412 batted balls; home over 1,119 batted balls); a gap of 7.3 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 6.5 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 66fd4a5e38e890fd.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the lineup facing the one-pitch-heavy starter reaches base against him at or above the league rate starters allow -- predictability showing up as production
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 49.2%, home 27.4% (this game's own values rest on: away over 8,178 pitches; home over 5,303 pitches); a gap of 21.8 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 16.3 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 11da2d044a08ac38.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the harder-throwing starter -- the one this side is backed BECAUSE its opponent has to face him -- holds that opposing lineup below the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (starter_velocity_gap; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away -0.52 mph, home 2.61 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 179 measured fastballs; home over 156 measured fastballs); a gap of 3.13 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. thesis: Backing the away side of the first-five-innings moneyline because 2 pre-registered signals fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 49.2%, home 27.4% (this game's own values rest on: away over 8,178 pitches; home over 5,303 pitches); a gap of 21.8 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 9.7 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. (2) how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (starter_velocity_gap; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away -0.52 mph, home 2.61 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 179 measured fastballs; home over 156 measured fastballs); a gap of 3.13 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. Its p_model is the board's own de-vigged consensus for this exact selection, republished unchanged by analyze()'s PROJECT phase under the identity map -- zero fitted parameters, no recalibration intercept, no Platt, no isotonic refit (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md §2). It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

Its p_model is the board's own de-vigged consensus for this exact selection, republished unchanged by analyze()'s PROJECT phase under the identity map -- zero fitted parameters, no recalibration intercept, no Platt, no isotonic refit (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md §2). Because the probability IS the price, diffing the two would measure nothing: edge_bps is structurally None and no edge is claimed. It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

counterarguments.detail: DEGRADED_INFORMATION: away_lineup: not present in assumption_exposure

thesis: This is a DELIBERATE CONTROL, not a pick anyone should follow: it takes the home side of the run line in every game, always, on no information at all. mechanism_predicates.claim: the lineup facing the one-pitch-heavy starter reaches base against him at or above the league rate starters allow -- predictability showing up as production
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 36.6%, home 60.8% (this game's own values rest on: away over 3,541 pitches; home over 268 pitches); a gap of 24.2 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 16.3 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 11da2d044a08ac38.)

Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome e64c85130b4664cc.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the lineup facing the one-pitch-heavy starter reaches base against him at or above the league rate starters allow -- predictability showing up as production
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 36.6%, home 60.8% (this game's own values rest on: away over 3,541 pitches; home over 268 pitches); a gap of 24.2 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 16.3 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 11da2d044a08ac38.)

thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) this lineup's top-of-order minus bottom-of-order strength (top_minus_bottom; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.029 wOBA, home 0.004 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 6,965 plate-appearance denominators; home over 3,384 plate-appearance denominators); a gap of 0.025 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.023 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,838 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a top-heavy order concentrates its best bats where the extra plate appearances go, and club-level pricing averages that concentration away; the weakest mechanism of the six, kept because V4 stated it before seeing its result. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. mechanism_predicates.claim: the lineup facing the one-pitch-heavy starter reaches base against him at or above the league rate starters allow -- predictability showing up as production
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 36.6%, home 60.8% (this game's own values rest on: away over 3,541 pitches; home over 268 pitches); a gap of 24.2 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 16.3 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 11da2d044a08ac38.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the lineup facing the one-pitch-heavy starter reaches base against him at or above the league rate starters allow -- predictability showing up as production
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 36.6%, home 60.8% (this game's own values rest on: away over 3,541 pitches; home over 268 pitches); a gap of 24.2 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 16.3 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 11da2d044a08ac38.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the lineup facing the one-pitch-heavy starter reaches base against him at or above the league rate starters allow -- predictability showing up as production
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 36.6%, home 60.8% (this game's own values rest on: away over 3,541 pitches; home over 268 pitches); a gap of 24.2 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 16.3 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 11da2d044a08ac38.)

mechanism_predicates.claim: the lineup facing the one-pitch-heavy starter reaches base against him at or above the league rate starters allow -- predictability showing up as production
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 36.6%, home 60.8% (this game's own values rest on: away over 3,541 pitches; home over 268 pitches); a gap of 24.2 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 16.3 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 11da2d044a08ac38.)

This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. mechanism_predicates.claim: the harder-throwing starter -- the one this side is backed BECAUSE its opponent has to face him -- holds that opposing lineup below the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (starter_velocity_gap; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away -0.91 mph, home 1.48 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 219 measured fastballs; home over 267 measured fastballs); a gap of 2.39 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 44faa9639a3a54e8.)

mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_batted_balls

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (starter_groundball_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 54.9%, home 40.6% (this game's own values rest on: away over 1,541 batted balls; home over 1,846 batted balls); a gap of 14.3 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 11.6 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. mechanism_predicates.claim: the ground-ball starter this side is backed behind actually pitched to the ground, at or above the league share of unambiguous batted-ball outs
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_batted_balls

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (starter_groundball_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 54.9%, home 40.6% (this game's own values rest on: away over 1,541 batted balls; home over 1,846 batted balls); a gap of 14.3 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 11.6 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 44faa9639a3a54e8.)

mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (starter_velocity_gap; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 4.14 mph, home 0.33 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 178 measured fastballs; home over 206 measured fastballs); a gap of 3.81 mph, clearing the threshold of 3.38 mph (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 375833d79e4bfef1.)

This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. mechanism_predicates.claim: the harder-throwing starter -- the one this side is backed BECAUSE its opponent has to face him -- holds that opposing lineup below the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (starter_velocity_gap; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 6.67 mph, home 2.93 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 254 measured fastballs; home over 253 measured fastballs); a gap of 3.74 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 44faa9639a3a54e8.)

mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_lineup_vs_opposing_starter

thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 61.1%, home 33.6% (this game's own values rest on: away over 3,917 pitches; home over 9,384 pitches); a gap of 27.5 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 16.3 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 11da2d044a08ac38.)

thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (primary_pitch_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 61.1%, home 33.6% (this game's own values rest on: away over 3,917 pitches; home over 9,384 pitches); a gap of 27.5 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 23.1 percentage points (rung 3 of 3, the 90th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. thesis: Backing the home side of the first-five-innings moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (starter_velocity_gap; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 6.67 mph, home 2.93 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 254 measured fastballs; home over 253 measured fastballs); a gap of 3.74 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome b0f7d329342ebce1.)

This pick carries the market's own probability and no edge, by construction. Its p_model is the board's own de-vigged consensus for this exact selection, republished unchanged by analyze()'s PROJECT phase under the identity map -- zero fitted parameters, no recalibration intercept, no Platt, no isotonic refit (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md §2). Because the probability IS the price, diffing the two would measure nothing: edge_bps is structurally None and no edge is claimed. It is published as a calibration reference -- how good the market's own number is -- never as a reason to bet.

mechanism_predicates.claim: the ground-ball starter this side is backed behind actually pitched to the ground, at or above the league share of unambiguous batted-ball outs
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_batted_balls

mechanism_predicates.claim: the harder-throwing starter -- the one this side is backed BECAUSE its opponent has to face him -- holds that opposing lineup below the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 2 pre-registered signals fired: (1) the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (starter_groundball_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 30.0%, home 50.2% (this game's own values rest on: away over 313 batted balls; home over 1,134 batted balls); a gap of 20.2 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 11.6 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. (2) how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (starter_velocity_gap; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away -0.61 mph, home 2.07 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 213 measured fastballs; home over 173 measured fastballs); a gap of 2.68 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 44faa9639a3a54e8.)

mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_batted_balls

mechanism_predicates.claim: the harder-throwing starter -- the one this side is backed BECAUSE its opponent has to face him -- holds that opposing lineup below the league rate starters allow
mechanism_predicates.subject: backed_starter_vs_opposing_lineup

thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 2 pre-registered signals fired: (1) the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (starter_groundball_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 30.0%, home 50.2% (this game's own values rest on: away over 313 batted balls; home over 1,134 batted balls); a gap of 20.2 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 11.6 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. (2) how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (starter_velocity_gap; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away -0.61 mph, home 2.07 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 213 measured fastballs; home over 173 measured fastballs); a gap of 2.68 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned. (Strategy: evolab genome 44faa9639a3a54e8.)

thesis: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 2 pre-registered signals fired: (1) the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (starter_groundball_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 30.0%, home 50.2% (this game's own values rest on: away over 313 batted balls; home over 1,134 batted balls); a gap of 20.2 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 11.6 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. (2) how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (starter_velocity_gap; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away -0.61 mph, home 2.07 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 213 measured fastballs; home over 173 measured fastballs); a gap of 2.68 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned.
